# Northstar — Monday Business Review: Product & Growth analysis

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

1. **The headline revenue growth is an artefact.** Raw October invoicing is €892.9k vs €797.1k in September (+12%). Strip out a duplicate invoice (€19.5k), an annual pre-payment booked at full value (€110k excess), and non-recurring professional services, and recurring revenue grew **€746.1k → €757.7k (+1.6%)**. After the five October churns, the November run-rate starting point is **€732.4k — below September**.
2. **Churn just spiked.** 5 of 31 customers active on 1 October churned (16% logo churn in one month): 4 of 9 starter customers (44%) plus Nakatomi (Mid-market Pro, €180k ARR). All five showed a ~16–37% usage drop in October and most had unresolved high-severity `api_errors` tickets. The €25.3k MRR lost is more than double the €11.1k MRR from October's five new logos.
3. **Soylent (€234k ARR) is the next churn risk**: usage −27%, downgraded €22k → €19.5k/month, and 8 tickets in October including a critical `api_errors`. **Wayne Enterprises (€1.008M ARR) renews 30 November** with recurring high-severity `api_errors`/`performance` tickets in both months.
4. **Acme's −45% request drop is not a churn signal** — it matches the planned batch migration (40–50% expected); tokens −12%, users 240→232, tickets fell 4→3 with none high-severity. But it mechanically drags the Enterprise plan's average usage down and masks +8% underlying growth.
5. **Paid search's "€238.8k attributed" is not evidence to increase spend.** €174k of it is last-touch-attributed expansion from customers acquired in 2023–24, none of which is yet visible in invoices or ARR. New-logo ARR from paid search over two months is €64.8k. Lead-to-trial fell from 8.5% to 6.4% as volume grew 73%. **CAC and payback cannot be calculated — there is no spend data in the pack.**
6. **Pro is the strongest plan on economics** (~63% margin) and shows clear unmet demand (3 customers over the 600k included requests; rate-limit tickets 5 → 13). Enterprise margin compressed 32.2% → 29.5% on flat revenue. Starter is marginal (32%) and shrinking in ACV.

---

## 2. REVENUE & CUSTOMER HEALTH

### 2.1 Reconciling the headline

| | Sept | Oct | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Raw invoices as loaded | 797,100 | 892,900 | +12.0% |
| Remove duplicate INV-2026-10-0209 (Soylent, `billing_sync`) | 797,100 | 873,400 | +9.6% |
| Normalise Gringotts annual (€120k → €10k monthly-equivalent) | 797,100 | 763,400 | −4.2% |
| Remove professional services (€51k Sept: Globex 33k, Hooli 18k; €5.7k Oct: Aperture) | **746,100** | **757,700** | **+1.6%** |

The recurring figures reconcile exactly to `plans.csv` (659,000+63,000+24,100 = 746,100; 659,500+66,200+32,000 = 757,700), which confirms plans.csv is already MRR-normalised while revenue.csv is not.

### 2.2 MRR bridge Sept → Oct (+€11,600)

- New logos (Oct): Spacely 3,200 + Cogswell 2,100 + Bishop 1,700 + Gekko 2,200 + Paper Street 1,900 = **+11,100**
- Expansion: Hooli 18,000 → 21,000 = **+3,000** (matches acquisition.csv's €36k ARR attribution)
- Contraction: Soylent 22,000 → 19,500 = **−2,500**
- Net = +11,600 ✓

**Not yet in the bridge but already known:**
- Churned in October after being invoiced 1 Oct: Nakatomi 15,000 + Slate Rock 2,000 + Mega-Lo-Mart 2,700 + Dinoco 2,300 + Buy N Large 3,300 = **−25,300** → November starting MRR ≈ **€732,400** (−1.8% vs Sept).
- October expansions in acquisition.csv (Stark 7,000, Umbrella 4,000, Globex 3,500, Massive Dynamic 1,500, Cyberdyne 2,000 = +18,000/month) "take effect from the following billing cycle". If they land, November ≈ €750k — roughly flat with September. None are reflected in `arr_eur` yet, so they are unverified.

### 2.3 Segment view

| Segment | Customers | Oct MRR | Share | Post-churn MRR | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise | 8 | 565,000 | 74.6% | 565,000 | ARR €6.78M; zero movement in 2 months |
| Mid-market | 10 → 9 | 142,500 | 18.8% | 127,500 | Nakatomi churned; Soylent contracted & at risk; Hooli expanded; Gringotts moved to annual |
| SMB | 18 → 14 | 50,200 | 6.6% | 39,900 | 4 starter churns; 5 new logos smaller than those lost |

**Concentration:** 8 logos = 75% of MRR; Stark + Wayne + Acme alone = €257k/month (34%). Wayne renews 30 Nov and has open/pending high-severity tickets.

### 2.4 Churn signals were visible in the data

| Customer | Plan | Usage Δ Oct | Tickets | Churn date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nakatomi | Pro | −16.1% | High api_errors Sept & Oct (Oct open) | 19 Oct |
| Slate Rock | Starter | −34.7% | High api_errors Sept (open), Oct | 8 Oct |
| Mega-Lo-Mart | Starter | −37.1% | billing pending | 15 Oct |
| Dinoco | Starter | −35.5% | High api_errors Oct | 22 Oct |
| Buy N Large | Starter | −37.0% | billing | 27 Oct |

Every non-churned starter customer grew 8–53%. A ~35% same-month drop clustered in one cohort (all acquired 2024–2025, all churning in October) points to a shared cause — reliability (`api_errors`) or a renewal/billing event — that the pack cannot identify. The four starter churns had average ARR €30.9k; the four October starter new logos average €23.7k, so replacement logos are ~25% smaller.

**Soylent** should be treated as an active save: tickets 3 → 8 (1 critical, 3 high api_errors, 2 high performance), usage −27%, active users 56 → 41, already contracted €30k ARR. Renewal is May 2027 but the pattern mirrors Nakatomi.

### 2.5 Usage health once Acme is excluded

Enterprise-plan requests: 26.54M → 26.44M (−0.4%). Excluding Acme: 22.34M → 24.13M (**+8.0%**). All Enterprise-segment customers other than Acme grew 5–10%; Mid-market on enterprise plan grew 9–22% except Soylent. Stark (4.29M) and Wayne (3.41M) exceed the 3M included volume — overage will be billed at renewal (Wayne's is in 4 weeks). Acme's migration takes it under the cap (2.31M), which may reduce overage revenue at its Feb 2027 renewal.

### 2.6 Support load

Tickets 59 → 74 (+25%); high/critical 16 → 20. By plan: enterprise 33 → 35, **pro 19 → 28 (+47%)**, starter 7 → 11. Rate-limit tickets 5 → 13, all on Pro.

---

## 3. ACQUISITION

### 3.1 What the funnel shows

| Channel | Leads S→O | Trials S→O | Lead→trial S→O |
|---|---|---|---|
| paid_search | 520 → 900 (+73%) | 44 → 58 (+32%) | 8.5% → **6.4%** |
| content | 260 → 330 | 31 → 34 | 11.9% → 10.3% |
| partner | 60 → 75 | 15 → 17 | 25.0% → 22.7% |
| outbound | 160 → 195 | 10 → 11 | 6.3% → 5.6% |

Every channel's lead-to-trial rate fell; paid search fell most while scaling most — consistent with lower-quality incremental leads, though two months cannot prove it.

### 3.2 What the attribution file shows

Attributed ARR by channel, split by type:

| Channel | New-logo ARR (2 mo) | Logos | Expansion ARR attributed | Verified in invoices? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| partner | 166,800 | 2 (Vandelay 132k, Clampett 34.8k) | 0 | Yes |
| content | 91,200 | 3 | 18,000 (Massive Dynamic) | New logos yes; expansion no |
| paid_search | 64,800 | 2 (Spacely, Gekko) | 210,000 (Hooli 36k ✓, Stark 84k, Umbrella 48k, Globex 42k) | Only Hooli |
| outbound | 56,400 | 2 | 24,000 (Cyberdyne) | New logos yes; expansion no |

Paid search's October total of €238.8k is 73% expansion from customers acquired in 2023–2024, attributed to a campaign that started 28 September and "converted" 2–4 weeks later. Those expansions have not yet produced an invoice or an `arr_eur` change (Stark's ARR is still exactly 95,000 × 12). Crediting a 3-year-old enterprise account's upsell to a paid-search click is a last-touch artefact, not evidence of channel effectiveness.

### 3.3 What cannot be concluded

- **CAC / CAC payback by channel: not computable.** No channel spend exists anywhere in the pack. The CFO's request cannot be answered without a spend file.
- **Trial-to-paid conversion: not tracked.** 44 paid-search trials in September produced zero new logos in either month; 15 partner trials produced 2 logos worth €166.8k. Whether that gap is lag or quality is unknowable from this data.
- **Retention by channel: not computable.** The five churned customers predate the acquisition file, so we cannot tell which channel sourced them.
- Partner delivers the highest lead-to-trial rate and the highest new-logo ARR, but from 60–75 leads/month — scalability is unknown.

**Conclusion:** the data does not support increasing paid-search spend. It also does not support cutting it. It supports getting spend, trial-to-paid, and a cleaner attribution rule before any reallocation.

---

## 4. PLAN ECONOMICS

### 4.1 Contribution by plan

| Plan | Month | Cust. | Revenue | Infra | Support | Contribution | Margin | Rev/cust | Cost/cust |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise | Sept | 14 | 659,000 | 288,000 | 159,000 | 212,000 | 32.2% | 47,071 | 31,929 |
| Enterprise | Oct | 14 | 659,500 | 296,800 | 168,000 | **194,700** | **29.5%** | 47,107 | 33,200 |
| Pro | Sept | 8 | 63,000 | 13,600 | 6,900 | 42,500 | 67.5% | 7,875 | 2,563 |
| Pro | Oct | 9 | 66,200 | 16,100 | 8,600 | **41,500** | **62.7%** | 7,356 | 2,744 |
| Starter | Sept | 9 | 24,100 | 8,400 | 7,300 | 8,400 | 34.9% | 2,678 | 1,744 |
| Starter | Oct | 13 | 32,000 | 11,400 | 10,300 | **10,300** | **32.2%** | 2,462 | 1,669 |

Enterprise delivers 79% of contribution but its margin fell 2.7 pts: costs +€17.8k (+4%) on +€500 revenue. Infra cost per customer rose while average requests were flat — driven partly by token growth (+~5% ex-Acme) and partly unexplained.

### 4.2 Pro — strongest, and hitting its ceiling

- Highest margin by a wide margin; per-customer cost is ~1/12 of Enterprise for ~1/6 the revenue.
- Usage growth Oct: Aperture +21.6%, Vandelay +32.7%, Prestige +13.5%, Wonka +13.3%, Planet Express +49.3% — every active Pro customer except Nakatomi grew ≥9%.
- Three customers exceed the 600k included requests: **Wonka 1.02M (170%)**, Aperture 705k (118%), Vandelay 690k (115%). Overage is only billed at renewal, so this demand is producing rate-limit tickets today and no revenue until 2027.
- Rate-limit tickets 5 → 13; Pro tickets per customer 3.1/month vs 2.5 (Enterprise) and 0.8 (Starter) — yet Pro's allocated support cost is only €8.6k. Either Pro is under-served or its cost allocation understates the true cost (see §6).
- Nakatomi's churn (€180k ARR, high api_errors both months) is the caution: Pro customers outgrowing the plan without a path forward leave.

### 4.3 Starter — weakest

- 32% margin on €32k revenue; €10.3k contribution for 13 customers.
- Plans.csv still counts the 4 churned customers; on 9 remaining customers November starter revenue is ~€21.7k, below September.
- Average usage per customer fell 114k → 84k because new logos are small (33–46k requests) — 20% of the included 200k. New starter logos are smaller in ACV than those lost.
- Two months, 4 churns, no clear cause. Starter is a small P&L line either way (€10k/month contribution).

### 4.4 Enterprise — largest, margin under pressure, reliability recurring

Every Enterprise-segment customer except Acme and Globex raised a high-severity `api_errors` ticket in both months (Stark's is open, Contoso's is open, Wayne's performance ticket pending). This is systemic, not customer-specific, and it is the plan carrying 87% of revenue and the imminent Wayne renewal.

---

## 5. RECOMMENDATIONS

**Decision 1 — Reduce investment in one segment?**
*Not supported as framed.* Nothing in the data argues for cutting Enterprise or Mid-market. There is a partial case against **Starter (SMB)**: thin margin, shrinking ACV, 44% logo churn in one month. But the churn cluster is unexplained, the sample is 9 customers over 2 months, and Starter costs only ~€22k/month to run. Recommended action: freeze incremental Starter acquisition spend until the October churn cause is diagnosed (exit reasons, whether `api_errors` was the trigger, whether a renewal or price event coincided), rather than a structural cut. Redirect that attention to the SMB **Pro** accounts, which are the healthy part of SMB.

**Decision 2 — Increase spend on one acquisition channel?**
*Not supported.* Paid search's case rests on €174k of unverified, last-touch-attributed enterprise expansion; its incremental leads convert to trial less well; and there is no spend data to compute CAC. Before any reallocation: (a) get channel spend for Sept–Oct; (b) get trial-to-paid outcomes for the Sept trial cohort; (c) adopt an attribution rule that excludes expansion from accounts older than, say, 12 months from new-business channel credit. If a reallocation must happen this week, the data most supports a modest test of **partner** capacity (best lead-to-trial, best new-logo ARR), not paid search.

**Decision 3 — Which plan gets engineering focus?**
*Pro*, with one non-negotiable cross-plan item.
- Pro: build a self-serve overage/limit-raise mechanism and a Pro → Enterprise upgrade path; bill overage monthly rather than at renewal. Wonka, Aperture and Vandelay are the immediate expansion pipeline (~€300k combined ARR at risk of Nakatomi-style attrition if ignored).
- Cross-plan: the recurring high-severity `api_errors` pattern across Enterprise and the churned cohort is the single largest revenue risk in the pack. It should be root-caused this quarter regardless of plan focus.
- Do not put engineering into Starter until the churn is understood.

**Immediate account actions (this week)**
1. Wayne Enterprises (€1.008M, renews 30 Nov): executive review; resolve pending high-severity performance ticket; agree overage treatment (3.41M vs 3M included) before it becomes a renewal objection.
2. Soylent (€234k): save plan — 8 tickets, critical api_errors, −27% usage, already downgraded.
3. Stark, Contoso: close the open high-severity api_errors tickets.
4. Verify the five October expansions in acquisition.csv are actually contracted and will invoice in November.

**Data fixes before next review**
- Dedupe revenue.csv on `transaction_id`; exclude `billing_sync` rows where a `stripe` row exists.
- Report recurring revenue on a monthly-equivalent basis (use `billing_period_months`) and separate professional services.
- Add churn status to plans.csv counts.
- Add channel spend and trial-to-paid outcomes; then CAC payback can be produced.

---

## 6. UNCERTAINTIES / DATA ISSUES

1. **Duplicate invoice** — INV-2026-10-0209 (Soylent, €19,500) appears twice (`stripe` and `billing_sync`). Inflates October by €19.5k if not deduplicated.
2. **Annual pre-payment booked at full value** — Gringotts €120,000 for 12 months dated 1 Oct. Inflates October by €110k vs monthly-equivalent; will depress the next 11 months unless normalised.
3. **Professional services** (€51k Sept vs €5.7k Oct) are non-recurring and distort month-on-month comparisons.
4. **Identifier mismatch** — `wayne-enterprises`↔`wayne_ent`, `prestige-worldwide`↔`prestige_ww`. Joins on `customer_id` would silently drop two customers (one is €1M ARR); use `usage_account_id`.
5. **Acme's −45% requests is planned**, not organic; it pulls `avg_requests_per_customer` for Enterprise negative when underlying growth is +8%. Tokens (−12%) are the better measure of Acme's real activity.
6. **plans.csv counts churned customers** in October (36 vs 31 going forward). Starter is 9 customers, not 13; Pro is 8, not 9.
7. **Attributed expansion revenue is unverified** — €216k ARR of October expansions have no invoice and no `arr_eur` change. Either `arr_eur` is stale or the bookings are not yet contracted. Hooli (Sept) is the only expansion confirmed in invoices.
8. **Attribution methodology** — crediting 2023–24 enterprise accounts' expansion to a campaign started days earlier is last-touch; no causal claim is supportable.
9. **No channel spend** → CAC, CAC payback, and ROI by channel cannot be computed. No trial-to-paid data → funnel efficiency stops at trial.
10. **Costs are by plan, not by segment** — segment profitability (the Finance question) cannot be measured directly; Mid-market spans two plans.
11. **Pro support cost may be understated** — Pro generates 38% of tickets on 5% of support cost. If CS time is actually flowing to Pro accounts, Pro's 63% margin is overstated.
12. **Churn cause is unknown** — no exit reasons; the co-occurrence of usage drops and api_errors tickets is correlation only. Whether October invoices to churned customers were refunded is not recorded.
13. **Two months of data** — no seasonality baseline, no trend; every rate of change here is a single observation.
14. **Rate-limit tickets from customers well under the monthly included volume** (Planet Express 112k, Pied Piper 186k) suggest limits are also per-second/burst, which the plan definition does not describe.
15. **Date inconsistency** — the pack describes October 2026 as complete while today's system date is 2 September 2026; the pack has been taken at face value, but the timestamping should be checked.
